summary: Canary traffic drain timing exposed fallback routing and removed active pin during version-freeze window
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled version-freeze window for AcmeHealth's dedicated pool, canary drain timing aligned with a rolling-control check which caused active version pins to be considered stale by the routing cache. Impact: ~6% of requests observed fallback to a lower-capacity model variant for ~7 minutes. Customer saw increased p50/p95 latency and 5xx uplift on mixed workloads. Business impact: degraded user experience for production medical triage feature; contractual SLA risk.

Observed behavior: Pin listed in customer config (model_version: redwood-stable-2026-02) was reported as active in the control plane, but runtime routing tables routed a fraction of traffic to a fallback variant during the drain step of a canary, effectively bypassing the pin for ephemeral requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have a dedicated pool with model pin configured at project level. 2) Start a canary rollout of a minor quantized variant with drain steps enabled. 3) Trigger a controlled drain (canary weight decrement). 4) Observe routing decisions in the period immediately after drain start (0-10s window) for requests using pinned model_version header. 5) Reproduce with traffic shaped to include long-context prompts to exercise KV cache behavior.
logs:
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] router: route-eval request_id=abc123 pin=redwood-stable-2026-02 decision=FALLBACK reason=drain_overlap
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] serving-runtime: selection openlm-v2-13b-quant fallback assigned node=dedicated-gpu-7
[2026-03-09T14:29:12Z] metrics: p95_latency +320ms baseline, errors 5xx increased from 0.2% to 1.8%
Conversation logs and helm: slack:#support-acmehealth thread t=165278, incident: INC-2026-03-09-AH
investigation_notes: Initial triage: routing decision contained 'drain_overlap' tag — indicates count-based canary drain interacted with pin TTLs in routing cache.
Control-plane showed the customer's pin still active and the intended pinned modelVersion in the account config, no manual unpin observed.

Routing cache entries for pinned routes have a short eviction TTL (default 8s) to allow rollouts to propagate quickly; during the canary weight change there was a race where caches were refreshed and observed partial canary state leading to fallback path selection.
Dedicated autoscaler and pool churn logs showed a single transient worker reboot (dedicated-gpu-7) ~14:22 which may have amplified fallback selection probability when combined with cache refresh.

Hypothesis: timing window between canary drain start and cache stabilization allowed route-eval to match canary-side rule before the pin-matching rule was re-evaluated, causing ephemeral bypass of explicit pining policy.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Raised by customer during on-call callback. Included p95 graphs and request ids.
AcmeHealth (Customer): Noted that this happened during a maintenance window and that they expect pins to be preserved during freezes — asked for immediate mitigation and root cause.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reproduced locally by simulating drain timing; confirmed route-eval sequence where canary rule evaluated before persistent-pin lookup when cache miss occurred.
Eng (Release team): Noted a similar edge case in router PR discussion but believed cache TTL prevented it — will re-evaluate decision order.
Support (Aisha): Applied emergency mitigation: pinned a hard route override at the edge for AcmeHealth tenant and confirmed no further fallbacks observed.
resolution: Mitigated: applied tenant-scoped hard route override to enforce model_version pin at edge for AcmeHealth (manual policy) which prevented further fallbacks during the maintenance window. Patch planned: change router evaluation order so persistent pin lookups are authoritative even when routing cache misses occur during canary drain steps. Backport to release-manager and router for Dedicated.
workaround: Support can apply a tenant-scoped route override (console -> routing -> overrides) to hard-enforce model_version while a rollout/drain is happening. For customers on Dedicated, request temporary increase of routing-cache TTL as stop-gap. Manual instruction provided to AcmeHealth in Slack channel.
root_cause: Race condition in routing evaluation: when the routing cache experienced transient misses during a canary drain, canary rules were evaluated before authoritative pin lookup, allowing fallback policies to apply. Amplified by a transient dedicated worker reboot which increased fallback probability.
followup_actions: ENG-1243: Update routing evaluation flow so persistent pin lookup occurs prior to canary rule application on cache miss (owner: router-team).
ENG-1244: Add integration test simulating canary drain + pin TTLs under transient worker restarts (owner: rollout-team).
OPS-532: Create runbook shortcut for tenant-scoped hard overrides and publish to Support runbooks.
Release: Backport fix to 2026-02 stable branch and schedule hotfix deploy to Dedicated control plane in us-west-2.
